events.title: The martyrdom of Archbishop Óscar Romero
events.shortBlurb: The archbishop of San Salvador was shot dead at the altar the day after pleading with soldiers to stop killing their people…
body: Born on 15 August 1917 at Ciudad Barrios and ordained in Rome in 1942, Óscar Romero was named archbishop of San Salvador on 23 February 1977, a safe and bookish choice, it was thought. The murder, three weeks later, of his friend the Jesuit Rutilio Grande changed him: his Sunday homilies, broadcast nationwide, began to name the dead, the tortured, and the disappeared of El Salvador's gathering war.

On 23 March 1980, in his last broadcast homily, he appealed to the soldiers: 'I beg you, I beseech you, I order you, in the name of God: stop the repression.' The next evening, 24 March, a single gunman shot him through the heart as he celebrated Mass in the chapel of the hospital of La Divina Providencia, where he lived.

At his funeral in the cathedral, gunfire into the mourning crowd left some thirty dead. A United Nations truth commission later blamed the death-squad leader Roberto D'Aubuisson for ordering his murder. Beatified in 2015, Romero was canonized by Pope Francis on 14 October 2018 — a bishop martyred at the altar for the faith he preached.

sources.text: Vatican biography, Canonization of St. Óscar Romero (vatican.va)
